gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much of the rated 25 W each cooled mount actually kept up over 30 minutes, or how many watts each one turns into heat instead of charge. From MobileReviews Eh!'s raw numbers: ESR OmniLock 76% (19.1 W) with 6.7 W lost; LISEN 2E7179 76% with 7.4 W lost; Spigen Cryomax 75% but 14.5 W lost; Anker Prime A2933 only 47% (11.7 W).
standout_why: MobileReviews Eh! (Nov 7 2026, cited in two chats) publishes the inputs: watts into the battery averaged over 30 minutes, watts drawn, efficiency and peak surface temperature for 11 mounts. It does not show them as a share of the rated 25 W, as watts lost to heat, or as price per watt delivered. Mobileplustech (Oct 26 2026) has no measured figures and no prices. Macworld's car-charger guide has no test method; its only time-to-50% figure is an estimate for the Anker ('just over half an hour'). The math is new, but a reader of MobileReviews could do it in their head, so the gain is partial.
decides: Confirms ESR OmniLock CryoBoost as the pick for keeping close to full speed (76% of 25 W, lowest waste heat among the fastest three). LISEN 2E7179 matches it at about $2.10 per sustained watt against ESR's $2.98. It also undercuts the Anker Prime AirCool, which ChatGPT called the premium or 'max cooling' pick in four chats. Anker measured 47% of rated, which is $7.69 per sustained watt at today's $89.99 on anker.com. No independent watt figure exists for the UGREEN MagFlow Pro car charger (US SKU 75250), which ChatGPT called best value in three chats. The only UGREEN TEC-plus-fan vent mount tested (model W778) delivered 1.4 W and was disqualified. No source we opened says W778 and the MagFlow Pro are the same product.
